solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: English stigma made French scoff

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
a scar is a lasting mark of disgrace, a stigma
to get someone to do something is to make them, so made can be got

explanation.surface: An English disgrace provokes French mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like a verb meaning to jeer, but here it is the slang noun for food.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargots are snails, a classic dish of French cuisine, and scoff is informal British slang for food.

clue.text: Flash one's lower parts

parts.note: a flash is an instant, a second
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is read as is, joining the pieces

explanation.surface: Someone exposes their lower body parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' and 'lower parts' build an indecent-exposure picture; the lower parts are musical ones.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, secondi are the second or lower parts in a duet or ensemble, plural of the Italian secondo.

clue.text: Finally organising diverse people into rank and order

indicators.note: into says these letters go inside the following word

parts.note: rank and arrant both mean utter or downright

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: last letters of organising and diverse
men are people

explanation.surface: A manager finally sorts a mixed crowd into ranks and good order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a military row, but it is the adjective meaning utter.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement is an ordering of things, so the noun order is a synonym.

clue.text: Low spirits start to get lower?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of get
to lower (rhyming with tower) is to look threatening, to loom

explanation.surface: Feeling down at first, then sinking further?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' wants to be read as more low; it is the verb meaning to frown or threaten, said like flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloom is a state of sadness or depression, which is what low spirits means.

clue.text: Backer briefly entering explosive function

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so this piece is placed within the other

parts.note: TNT is a common explosive

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer, especially of a theatre show

explanation.surface: A financial sponsor is briefly caught up in an explosive party event.
explanation.definitionFit: The tangent is a trigonometric function, the ratio of the opposite side to the adjacent.

clue.text: Kindly feeding extremely suspicious bees etc

indicators.note: feeding means going into a mouth, so one piece is put inside another
extremely points to the extremities of the word, its two end letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of suspicious
a warm person is kindly and friendly

explanation.surface: A gentle person keeps feeding insects that are deeply suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees and other insects travel in swarms, so the plural noun describes groups of such creatures.

clue.text: Fancy Easter sun and sweet wine

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or decorated, so the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An invitation to enjoy spring sunshine with a glass of sweet wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet dessert wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: Sky broadcast quality song

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the open space above us
second meaning: to put out on radio or TV
third meaning: a manner or impression
fourth meaning: a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A satellite channel's broadcast of a high-quality song.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British TV broadcaster, which makes the four separate meanings read as one phrase about television.
explanation.definitionFit: The short word carries all four senses: the heavens, to transmit, an impression given off, and a tune.

clue.text: Mixture of male impetuosity and half-cut rage

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
elan is dash or impetuous vigour

indicators.note: half-cut means one half is chopped off, leaving only the back part

parts.note: the second half of rage

explanation.surface: Masculine recklessness mixed with drunken anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, which suits the surface; here it just halves the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A melange is a mixture or medley, from the French word for a blend.

clue.text: Eco-friendly vehicle part contains uranium, really oddly

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: contains says one word holds another within its letters

parts.note: the bonnet is part of a car, the British word for its hood
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in the odd-numbered positions only

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of really

explanation.surface: A green car has a part containing uranium, which would be odd indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vehicle part' reads as one idea but splits in two; the bonnet is the British name for a car's hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Something carbon neutral adds no net carbon dioxide to the atmosphere, which makes it environmentally friendly.

clue.text: Article about the setter's revolutionary nom de guerre

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: the setter refers to himself, so the setter's is my

explanation.surface: A piece about a revolutionary's alias, written by the crossword compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary nom de guerre' suggests a rebel's alias, but revolutionary only turns MY around.
explanation.definitionFit: An anonym is an assumed name, and a nom de guerre is a pseudonym, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Service is no good if earlier however

indicators.note: if earlier tells us the last phrase of the clue is placed in front rather than after

parts.note: even so means however, nevertheless
NG is the standard abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A church service is worthless if held earlier, though.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'no good, if however were earlier': EVEN SO is put before NG.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican service of evening prayer, so it is a church service.

clue.text: Queasy hosts digested last of blood pudding

indicators.note: hosts means takes in as guests, so the other letters go inside

parts.note: queasy means feeling sick
potted means summarised or condensed, as a digest is

indicators.note: last of takes only the final letter of the following word

parts.note: last letter of blood

explanation.surface: Someone queasy keeps down a black pudding they have eaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Spotted dick is a British steamed suet pudding with currants. 'Digested' suggests eating, but means summarised.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotted dick is a traditional British steamed dessert, so it is a pudding in the British sense of dessert.

clue.text: Weaselly type's rowdy intemperance leaving church

indicators.note: rowdy suggests disorder, so the remaining letters are jumbled
leaving means departing, so the letters for church are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A shifty character's drunken excess drives him out of church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weaselly type' hints at a sneaky person, but it is literally an animal of the weasel family.
explanation.definitionFit: The pine marten is a member of the weasel family (mustelids), a fair literal reading of weaselly type.

clue.text: Law firm exec regularly duped about new licence

indicators.note: regularly takes letters at even intervals, here every second one

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of law firm exec

indicators.note: about means around, so this word goes round the letter for new

parts.note: to be had is to be duped
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A law firm executive was regularly tricked over a new licence.
explanation.definitionFit: A free hand is freedom to act as one wishes, which is what licence means here.

clue.text: Left sweethearts to shed clothes

indicators.note: shedding clothes strips off the outside, so the outer letters are dropped

parts.note: sweethearts are lovers

explanation.surface: Abandoned couples resort to undressing.
explanation.walkthrough: LOVERS loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Over means left or remaining, as in food left over after a meal.

clue.text: Man perhaps read aloud passage

indicators.note: read aloud means we go by the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: an aisle is a passage between seats

explanation.surface: A man reads a passage out to an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man perhaps' is the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is one example of an isle, hence the perhaps signalling an example.

clue.text: Cunning insult overheard

indicators.note: overheard means caught by the ear, so we go by the sound

parts.note: a slight is an insult or snub

explanation.surface: A sly put-down that someone happened to overhear.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight means cunning or dexterity, as in sleight of hand, the noun use of cunning.

clue.text: Old story about India at back of Republican magazine

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps round the letter for India
at back of places this run of letters after the next piece

parts.note: Rep is the abbreviation for a US Republican
O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An old tale about India appears at the back of a Republican magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old story' looks like one unit, but Old gives just O, and I goes inside STORY after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine in the older sense is a storehouse, as for ammunition, and a repository is a place where things are stored.

clue.text: Garments putting pressure on navels

indicators.note: putting something on another places it above, first in a down entry

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
innies are navels that sink inwards, as opposed to outies

explanation.surface: Clothes that press tightly on the belly button.
explanation.walkthrough: Pinnies are pinafores, aprons worn over clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinny is an informal British word for a pinafore or apron, so pinnies are garments.

clue.text: Devoid of ego, listener somehow gives way

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive in some unstated order
devoid of means lacking, so the letter standing for ego is taken out

parts.note: I is the self, the ego
taken as written

explanation.surface: A humble listener somehow gives ground in an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften and yield, so relents means gives way.

clue.text: Tough old bird's lost after terrible tale

indicators.note: after says the bird follows the rearranged letters
terrible suggests something badly mangled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: has lost means a letter is taken away from the bird

parts.note: a heron is a wading bird
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A tough old bird has lost out after a dreadful story was told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough old bird' is a stock phrase for a hardy person, but Tough is the definition and the old belongs to the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathern means made of leather, and so figuratively tough and hard like leather.

clue.text: Former magistrate thought about limits of lenience

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: an idea is a thought

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its boundaries, its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of lenience

explanation.surface: A retired judge reflected on how far leniency should go.
explanation.definitionFit: An aedile was an official of ancient Rome in charge of public buildings and games, so a magistrate of the past.

clue.text: Silver pressing on primate's Christian love

indicators.note: pressing on means sitting on top, so this piece goes first in a down answer

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: Silver weighing down on an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' might suggest an archbishop, which suits Christian love, but here it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Agape is the Greek New Testament word for selfless, Christian love.

clue.text: A billion goats slaughtered for world economic development

indicators.note: slaughtered means cut to pieces, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mass cull of livestock is carried out in the name of world trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Globalisation is the growing integration of the world's economies through trade and investment.

clue.text: Confess some shallOW Notions

indicators.note: some means a portion, so the letters are a part of the words that follow

parts.note: the end of shallow and start of notions

explanation.surface: Admit to some superficial ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: To own, or own up, is to admit or confess something.

clue.text: Singular character departs on a trip

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for singular
the tone of something is its character or quality
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: An odd person sets off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On a trip' suggests travel, but here it is the drug-taker's trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stoned is high on drugs, and a trip is a drug-induced experience.

clue.text: Most stylish and vacuous supermodel, I'm afraid, is in France

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word loses all its inside letters

parts.note: supermodel emptied of its middle letters
eek is a cry of fright
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A shallow catwalk star in France is the chicest of all, I fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek means smooth and elegant, so the superlative means the most stylish.
